sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā mātā putram athābravīt nāndhaḥ kurūṇāṃ nṛpatir anurūpas tapodhana
english: Hearing those words of his, the mother then spoke to her son: 'A blind man is not a fitting king of the Kurus, O ascetic treasure.'

sanskrit: jñātivaṃśasya goptāraṃ pitṝṇāṃ vaṃśavardhanam dvitīyaṃ kuruvaṃśasya rājānaṃ dātum arhasi
english: 'You ought to give us another king — a protector of the kinsmen's lineage, an increaser of the ancestral line, a second king of the Kuru dynasty.'

sanskrit: sa tatheti pratijñāya niścakrāma mahātapāḥ sāpi kālena kausalyā suṣuve 'ndhaṃ tam ātmajam
english: He of great austerity promised 'So be it' and departed. And in time Kausalyā gave birth to that blind son.

sanskrit: punar eva tu sā devī paribhāṣya snuṣāṃ tataḥ ṛṣim āvāhayat satyā yathāpūrvam aninditā
english: But that blameless lady Satyavatī then instructed her daughter-in-law again and summoned the seer just as before.

sanskrit: tatas tenaiva vidhinā maharṣis tām apadyata ambālikām athābhyāgād ṛṣiṃ dṛṣṭvā ca sāpi tam viṣaṇṇā pāṇḍusaṃkāśā samapadyata bhārata
english: Then the great seer approached her by the same method. He came to Ambālikā, and she, upon seeing the seer, turned pale as a corpse, crestfallen, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tāṃ bhītāṃ pāṇḍusaṃkāśāṃ viṣaṇṇāṃ prekṣya pārthiva vyāsaḥ satyavatīputra idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing her frightened, pale as a corpse, and despondent, O king, Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī, spoke these words:

sanskrit: yasmāt pāṇḍutvam āpannā virūpaṃ prekṣya mām api tasmād eṣa sutas tubhyaṃ pāṇḍur eva bhaviṣyati
english: 'Because you turned pale upon seeing my hideous form, therefore this son of yours shall be named Pāṇḍu — pale indeed.'

sanskrit: nāma cāsya tad eveha bhaviṣyati śubhānane ity uktvā sa nirākrāmad bhagavān ṛṣisattamaḥ
english: 'And that very name shall be his in this world, O fair-faced one.' Having spoken thus, the blessed best of sages departed.

sanskrit: tato niṣkrāntam ālokya satyā putram abhāṣata śaśaṃsa sa punar mātre tasya bālasya pāṇḍutām
english: Then Satya, watching him depart, spoke to her son. He again reported to his mother the paleness of that child.

sanskrit: taṃ mātā punar evānyam ekaṃ putram ayācata tatheti ca maharṣis tāṃ mātaraṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: The mother begged him once more for yet another son. And the great seer replied to that mother, 'So be it.'

sanskrit: tataḥ kumāraṃ sā devī prāptakālam ajījanat pāṇḍuṃ lakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ dīpyamānam iva śriyā tasya putrā maheṣvāsā jajñire pañca pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Then in due time that princess gave birth to the boy Pāṇḍu, endowed with auspicious marks and blazing with glory. From him were born the five Pāṇḍavas, mighty archers all.

sanskrit: ṛtukāle tato jyeṣṭhāṃ vadhūṃ tasmai nyayojayat sā tu rūpaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca maharṣeḥ pravicintya tam nākarod vacanaṃ devyā bhayāt surasutopamā
english: Then at the fertile season she assigned the eldest daughter-in-law to him again. But that one, like the daughter of a god, reflecting on the seer’s appearance and smell, refused the queen's command out of fear.

sanskrit: tataḥ svair bhūṣaṇair dāsīṃ bhūṣayitvāpsaropamām preṣayām āsa kṛṣṇāya tataḥ kāśipateḥ sutā
english: Then the daughter of the king of Kāśī adorned a maidservant with her own ornaments, making her like an apsaras, and sent her to Kṛṣṇa (Vyāsa).

sanskrit: dāsī ṛṣim anuprāptaṃ pratyudgamyābhivādya ca saṃviveśābhyanujñātā satkṛtyopacacāra ha
english: The maidservant went forward to meet the seer as he arrived, greeted him reverently, and, given leave, lay with him and attended him with great care.

sanskrit: kāmopabhogena tu sa tasyāṃ tuṣṭim agād ṛṣiḥ tayā sahoṣito rātriṃ maharṣiḥ prīyamāṇayā
english: The seer found satisfaction in pleasure with her; the great seer passed the night dwelling with her, who was joyful.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhann abravīd enām abhujiṣyā bhaviṣyasi ayaṃ ca te śubhe garbhaḥ śrīmān udaram āgataḥ dharmātmā bhavitā loke sarvabuddhimatāṃ varaḥ
english: As he rose he said to her: 'You shall no longer be a slave. And this glorious child that has entered your womb, O auspicious one, shall be foremost among all the wise in the world, righteous in soul.'

sanskrit: sa jajñe viduro nāma kṛṣṇadvaipāyanātmajaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya ca bhrātā pāṇḍoś cāmitabuddhimān
english: He was born and was named Vidura — son of Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, brother of both Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Pāṇḍu, of boundless intelligence.

sanskrit: dharmo vidurarūpeṇa śāpāt tasya mahātmanaḥ māṇḍavyasyārthatattvajñaḥ kāmakrodhavivarjitaḥ
english: Dharma himself, by the curse of that great-souled Māṇḍavya, was born in the form of Vidura — knowing the truth of meaning, free from desire and anger.

sanskrit: sa dharmasyānṛṇo bhūtvā punar mātrā sametya ca tasyai garbhaṃ samāvedya tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Having discharged his debt to Dharma, he (Vyāsa) came once more to his mother and informed her of the birth, then vanished there and then.

sanskrit: evaṃ vicitravīryasya kṣetre dvaipāyanād api jajñire devagarbhābhāḥ kuruvaṃśavivardhanāḥ
english: Thus, in the field of Vicitravīrya, even from Dvaipāyana were born those who shone like the offspring of gods, the increasers of the Kuru lineage.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kiṃ kṛtaṃ karma dharmeṇa yena śāpam upeyivān kasya śāpāc ca brahmarṣe śūdrayonāv ajāyata
english: Janamejaya said: 'What deed did Dharma commit by which he incurred a curse? And by whose curse, O Brahmā-seer, was he born in a śūdra womb?'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca babhūva brāhmaṇaḥ kaś cin māṇḍavya iti viśrutaḥ dhṛtimān sarvadharmajñaḥ satye tapasi ca sthitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: 'There was a certain brahmin renowned as Māṇḍavya — steadfast, knowing all dharma, abiding in truth and austerity.'

sanskrit: sa āśramapadadvāri vṛkṣamūle mahātapāḥ ūrdhvabāhur mahāyogī tasthau maunavratānvitaḥ
english: He of great austerity stood at the gate of his hermitage at the root of a tree, arms raised, a great yogī, observing the vow of silence.

sanskrit: tasya kālena mahatā tasmiṃs tapasi tiṣṭhataḥ tam āśramapadaṃ prāptā dasyavo loptrahāriṇaḥ anusāryamāṇā bahubhī rakṣibhir bharatarṣabha
english: After a long time, while he stood thus in austerity, some robbers carrying stolen goods arrived at that hermitage, pursued by many guards, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: te tasyāvasathe loptraṃ nidadhuḥ kurusattama nidhāya ca bhayāl līnās tatraivānvāgate bale
english: They hid the plunder in his dwelling, O best of Kurus, and, having hidden it, crouched in concealment there when the troops arrived in pursuit.

sanskrit: teṣu līneṣv atho śīghraṃ tatas tad rakṣiṇāṃ balam ājagāma tato 'paśyaṃs tam ṛṣiṃ taskarānugāḥ
english: With the thieves thus hidden, the force of those guards quickly came there, and those trackers of thieves caught sight of that seer.

sanskrit: tam apṛcchaṃs tato rājaṃs tathāvṛttaṃ tapodhanam katareṇa pathā yātā dasyavo dvijasattama tena gacchāmahe brahman pathā śīghrataraṃ vayam
english: Then, O king, they questioned that treasure of austerity standing there: 'By which path did the robbers go, O best of twice-born? By that path, O brahmin, let us go with all speed.'

sanskrit: tathā tu rakṣiṇāṃ teṣāṃ bruvatāṃ sa tapodhanaḥ na kiṃ cid vacanaṃ rājann avadat sādhv asādhu vā
english: But that treasure of austerity, O king, though the guards were speaking thus, said not a word, neither good nor bad.

sanskrit: tatas te rājapuruṣā vicinvānās tadāśramam dadṛśus tatra saṃlīnāṃs tāṃś corān dravyam eva ca
english: Then those royal servants, searching through that hermitage, found the thieves hidden there, along with the goods themselves.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkā samabhavad rakṣiṇāṃ taṃ muniṃ prati saṃyamyainaṃ tato rājñe dasyūṃś caiva nyavedayan
english: Suspicion then arose among the guards against that sage; they bound him along with the thieves and reported everything to the king.

sanskrit: taṃ rājā saha taiś corair anvaśād vadhyatām iti sa vadhyaghātair ajñātaḥ śūle proto mahātapāḥ
english: The king ordered him to be executed along with those thieves. And that one of great austerity, unrecognised, was impaled upon a spike by the executioners.

sanskrit: tatas te śūlam āropya taṃ muniṃ rakṣiṇas tadā pratijagmur mahīpālaṃ dhanāny ādāya tāny atha
english: Then those guards, having raised that sage on the spike, went back to the king, taking those goods with them.

sanskrit: śūlasthaḥ sa tu dharmātmā kālena mahatā tataḥ nirāhāro 'pi viprarṣir maraṇaṃ nābhyupāgamat dhārayām āsa ca prāṇān ṛṣīṃś ca samupānayat
english: But that righteous soul, though impaled upon the spike, for a long time — without food, even — did not meet death, O brahmin-seer; he sustained his life-breath and drew other sages to him.

sanskrit: śūlāgre tapyamānena tapas tena mahātmanā saṃtāpaṃ paramaṃ jagmur munayo 'tha paraṃtapa
english: Through the austerity being performed by that great-souled one on the tip of the spike, the sages were overwhelmed with extreme distress, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: te rātrau śakunā bhūtvā saṃnyavartanta sarvataḥ darśayanto yathāśakti tam apṛcchan dvijottamam śrotum icchāmahe brahman kiṃ pāpaṃ kṛtavān asi
english: They became birds at night and gathered round from every side, showing themselves as best they could, and questioned that best of twice-born: 'We wish to hear, O brahmin, what sin you have committed.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sa muniśārdūlas tān uvāca tapodhanān doṣataḥ kaṃ gamiṣyāmi na hi me 'nyo 'parādhyati
english: Then that tiger among sages replied to those treasures of austerity: 'To what fault shall I trace it? For truly no other has wronged me.'

sanskrit: rājā ca tam ṛṣiṃ śrutvā niṣkramya saha mantribhiḥ prasādayām āsa tadā śūlastham ṛṣisattamam
english: And the king, hearing of that seer, came out with his ministers and then sought to propitiate that best of sages mounted on the spike.

sanskrit: yan mayāpakṛtaṃ mohād ajñānād ṛṣisattama prasādaye tvāṃ tatrāhaṃ na me tvaṃ kroddhum arhasi
english: 'Whatever wrong I did to you out of delusion and ignorance, O best of sages, I beg your forgiveness for that; you ought not be angry with me.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tato rājñā prasādam akaron muniḥ kṛtaprasādo rājā taṃ tataḥ samavatārayat
english: Addressed thus by the king, the sage showed grace. When he had received grace, the king then had him brought down from the spike.

sanskrit: avatārya ca śūlāgrāt tac chūlaṃ niścakarṣa ha aśaknuvaṃś ca niṣkraṣṭuṃ śūlaṃ mūle sa cicchide
english: Having brought him down from the spike's tip, they tried to pull out the spike. Being unable to extract it fully, they cut it at the base.

sanskrit: sa tathāntargatenaiva śūlena vyacaran muniḥ sa tena tapasā lokān vijigye durlabhān paraiḥ aṇīmāṇḍavya iti ca tato lokeṣu kathyate
english: That sage moved about with the spike still lodged inside him. By that austerity he conquered worlds difficult for others to attain. From then on he is known in the worlds as Aṇīmāṇḍavya — Spike-Māṇḍavya.

sanskrit: sa gatvā sadanaṃ vipro dharmasya paramārthavit āsanasthaṃ tato dharmaṃ dṛṣṭvopālabhata prabhuḥ
english: That brahmin, knowing the supreme truth, went to the abode of Dharma and, seeing Dharma seated there, reproached him, that powerful one.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tad duṣkṛtaṃ karma mayā kṛtam ajānatā yasyeyaṃ phalanirvṛttir īdṛśy āsāditā mayā śīghram ācakṣva me tattvaṃ paśya me tapaso balam
english: 'What evil deed was done by me unknowingly, whose fruit has been visited upon me in such a way? Tell me the truth quickly — see the power of my austerity.'

sanskrit: dharma uvāca pataṃgakānāṃ puccheṣu tvayeṣīkā praveśitā karmaṇas tasya te prāptaṃ phalam etat tapodhana
english: Dharma said: 'You once inserted straws into the tails of insects — the fruit of that deed has fallen upon you, O treasure of austerity.'

sanskrit: aṇīmāṇḍavya uvāca alpe 'parādhe vipulo mama daṇḍas tvayā kṛtaḥ śūdrayonāv ato dharma mānuṣaḥ saṃbhaviṣyasi
english: Aṇīmāṇḍavya said: 'For a trifling offence you have imposed a heavy punishment on me. Therefore, Dharma, you shall be born among men in a śūdra womb.'

sanskrit: maryādāṃ sthāpayāmy adya loke dharmaphalodayām ā caturdaśamād varṣān na bhaviṣyati pātakam pareṇa kurvatām evaṃ doṣa eva bhaviṣyati
english: 'I now establish this rule for the world regarding the arising of dharma's fruit: up to the fourteenth year of life there shall be no sin for those who do such things; beyond that it shall indeed be a transgression.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etena tv aparādhena śāpāt tasya mahātmanaḥ dharmo vidurarūpeṇa śūdrayonāv ajāyata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: 'It was by this offence, by the curse of that great-souled one, that Dharma was born in a śūdra womb in the form of Vidura.'

sanskrit: dharme cārthe ca kuśalo lobhakrodhavivarjitaḥ dīrghadarśī śamaparaḥ kurūṇāṃ ca hite rataḥ
english: Skilled in dharma and artha, free from greed and anger, far-sighted, devoted to tranquillity, and ever engaged in the welfare of the Kurus.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca teṣu triṣu kumāreṣu jāteṣu kurujāṅgalam kuravo 'tha kurukṣetraṃ trayam etad avardhata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: 'When those three princes were born, these three — Kuru-jāṅgala, the Kuru land, and Kuru-kṣetra — all flourished.'

sanskrit: ūrdhvasasyābhavad bhūmiḥ sasyāni phalavanti ca yathartuvarṣī parjanyo bahupuṣpaphalā drumāḥ
english: The earth bore crops standing tall; the harvests were fruitful; the rain-cloud rained according to the seasons; the trees were laden with many flowers and fruits.

sanskrit: vāhanāni prahṛṣṭāni muditā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ gandhavanti ca mālyāni rasavanti phalāni ca
english: The beasts of burden were exhilarated; the deer and birds were joyful; the garlands were fragrant; the fruits were full of flavour.

sanskrit: vaṇigbhiś cāvakīryanta nagarāṇy atha śilpibhiḥ śūrāś ca kṛtavidyāś ca santaś ca sukhino 'bhavan
english: The cities were filled with merchants and artisans; the brave, the learned, and the virtuous all lived happily.

sanskrit: nābhavan dasyavaḥ ke cin nādharmarucayo janāḥ pradeśeṣv api rāṣṭrāṇāṃ kṛtaṃ yugam avartata
english: There were no robbers, no people inclined to adharma; even in the outlying regions of the realm the Kṛta age prevailed.

sanskrit: dānakriyādharmaśīlā yajñavrataparāyaṇāḥ anyonyaprītisaṃyuktā vyavardhanta prajās tadā
english: The people, devoted to giving, righteous action, and dharma, intent on sacrifices and vows, bound to one another with affection, thrived in that time.

sanskrit: mānakrodhavihīnāś ca janā lobhavivarjitāḥ anyonyam abhyavardhanta dharmottaram avartata
english: People were free from pride and anger, rid of greed; they flourished with one another; dharma reigned supreme.

sanskrit: tan mahodadhivat pūrṇaṃ nagaraṃ vai vyarocata dvāratoraṇaniryūhair yuktam abhracayopamaiḥ prāsādaśatasaṃbādhaṃ mahendrapurasaṃnibham
english: That city shone, full like a great ocean, adorned with gateways, arches, and turrets like heaped clouds, crowded with hundreds of palaces, resembling the city of great Indra.

sanskrit: nadīṣu vanakhaṇḍeṣu vāpīpalvalasānuṣu kānaneṣu ca ramyeṣu vijahrur muditā janāḥ
english: People sported joyfully along rivers, in groves, on the banks of ponds and pools, and in pleasant forests.

sanskrit: uttaraiḥ kurubhiḥ sārdhaṃ dakṣiṇāḥ kuravas tadā vispardhamānā vyacaraṃs tathā siddharṣicāraṇaiḥ nābhavat kṛpaṇaḥ kaś cin nābhavan vidhavāḥ striyaḥ
english: The southern Kurus then ranged about rivalling the northern Kurus and also the Siddhas, sages, and Cāraṇas. There was no wretch, and women were not widowed.

sanskrit: tasmiñ janapade ramye bahavaḥ kurubhiḥ kṛtāḥ kūpārāmasabhāvāpyo brāhmaṇāvasathās tathā bhīṣmeṇa śāstrato rājan sarvataḥ parirakṣite
english: In that lovely land many wells, parks, assembly halls, ponds, and brahmin dwellings were built by the Kurus, and everything was guarded on all sides according to the śāstra by Bhīṣma, O king.

sanskrit: babhūva ramaṇīyaś ca caityayūpaśatāṅkitaḥ sa deśaḥ pararāṣṭrāṇi pratigṛhyābhivardhitaḥ bhīṣmeṇa vihitaṃ rāṣṭre dharmacakram avartata
english: That land was lovely, marked with hundreds of shrines and sacrificial posts, enlarged by the incorporation of neighbouring kingdoms; the wheel of dharma ordained by Bhīṣma turned in the realm.

sanskrit: kriyamāṇeṣu kṛtyeṣu kumārāṇāṃ mahātmanām paurajānapadāḥ sarve babhūvuḥ satatotsavāḥ
english: As the rites for those great-souled princes were being performed, all the citizens and country-folk were in a state of perpetual festival.

sanskrit: gṛheṣu kurumukhyānāṃ paurāṇāṃ ca narādhipa dīyatāṃ bhujyatāṃ ceti vāco 'śrūyanta sarvaśaḥ
english: In the houses of the leading Kurus and of the townspeople, O lord of men, the words 'Give! Eat!' were heard everywhere.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca pāṇḍuś ca viduraś ca mahāmatiḥ janmaprabhṛti bhīṣmeṇa putravat paripālitāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and the great-minded Vidura were all cared for from birth by Bhīṣma as though they were his own sons.

sanskrit: saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtās te tu vratādhyayanasaṃyutāḥ śramavyāyāmakuśalāḥ samapadyanta yauvanam
english: Consecrated with all rites, engaged in vows and Vedic study, skilled in exertion and exercise, they came to youth.

sanskrit: dhanurvede 'śvapṛṣṭhe ca gadāyuddhe 'sicarmaṇi tathaiva gajaśikṣāyāṃ nītiśāstre ca pāragāḥ
english: They became proficient in the science of archery, riding on horseback, fighting with the mace and sword-and-shield, likewise in the training of elephants, and in the science of statecraft.

sanskrit: itihāsapurāṇeṣu nānāśikṣāsu cābhibho vedavedāṅgatattvajñāḥ sarvatra kṛtaniśramāḥ
english: In histories and purāṇas, in various branches of learning, O lord, knowing the truth of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences — they applied themselves diligently in all.

sanskrit: pāṇḍur dhanuṣi vikrānto narebhyo 'bhyadhiko 'bhavat aty anyān balavān āsīd dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ
english: Pāṇḍu was surpassingly valiant with the bow, excelling all men; Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the earth, was stronger than all others.

sanskrit: triṣu lokeṣu na tv āsīt kaś cid vidurasaṃmitaḥ dharmanityas tato rājan dharme ca paramaṃ gataḥ
english: In all three worlds there was none equal to Vidura; ever fixed in dharma, O king, he had attained the highest in matters of dharma.

sanskrit: pranaṣṭaṃ śaṃtanor vaṃśaṃ samīkṣya punar uddhṛtam tato nirvacanaṃ loke sarvarāṣṭreṣv avartata
english: Seeing the line of Śaṃtanu, which had seemed lost, once more restored, this saying then spread through the world and all its kingdoms:

sanskrit: vīrasūnāṃ kāśisute deśānāṃ kurujāṅgalam sarvadharmavidāṃ bhīṣmaḥ purāṇāṃ gajasāhvayam
english: 'Of lands for the sons of heroes, Kuru-jāṅgala; of daughters of Kāśī for knowledge of all dharma; of ancient cities, the Elephant-named city (Hāstinapura) — Bhīṣma has established all these.'

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭras tv acakṣuṣṭvād rājyaṃ na pratyapadyata karaṇatvāc ca viduraḥ pāṇḍur āsīn mahīpatiḥ
english: But Dhṛtarāṣṭra did not obtain the kingdom on account of his blindness; and Vidura because he was born of a servant woman; Pāṇḍu became lord of the earth.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca guṇaiḥ samuditaṃ samyag idaṃ naḥ prathitaṃ kulam aty anyān pṛthivīpālān pṛthivyām adhirājyabhāk
english: Bhīṣma said: 'This family of ours, renowned and properly furnished with all virtues, holds sovereignty over the earth above all other kings of the earth.'

sanskrit: rakṣitaṃ rājabhiḥ pūrvair dharmavidbhir mahātmabhiḥ notsādam agamac cedaṃ kadā cid iha naḥ kulam
english: 'Protected by kings of old, those great souls who knew dharma, never at any time has our family come to ruin here.'

sanskrit: mayā ca satyavatyā ca kṛṣṇena ca mahātmanā samavasthāpitaṃ bhūyo yuṣmāsu kulatantuṣu
english: 'By me and by Satyavatī, and by the great-souled Kṛṣṇa (Vyāsa), it has been established once more in you, the threads of the lineage.'

sanskrit: vardhate tad idaṃ putra kulaṃ sāgaravad yathā tathā mayā vidhātavyaṃ tvayā caiva viśeṣataḥ
english: 'This family grows, my son, like the ocean. So it must be furthered by me and especially by you.'

sanskrit: śrūyate yādavī kanyā anurūpā kulasya naḥ subalasyātmajā caiva tathā madreśvarasya ca
english: 'It is heard that a Yādava princess suitable for our family, and likewise the daughter of Subala and the daughter of the lord of Madra —'

sanskrit: kulīnā rūpavatyaś ca nāthavatyaś ca sarvaśaḥ ucitāś caiva saṃbandhe te 'smākaṃ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: '— are well-born, beautiful, and possessed of worthy guardians in every way; they are fitting for alliance with us, those bulls among kṣatriyas.'

sanskrit: manye varayitavyās tā ity ahaṃ dhīmatāṃ vara saṃtānārthaṃ kulasyāsya yad vā vidura manyase
english: 'I think those women should be sought in marriage for the continuation of this family — O best of the wise, or else what do you think, Vidura?'

sanskrit: vidura uvāca bhavān pitā bhavān mātā bhavān naḥ paramo guruḥ tasmāt svayaṃ kulasyāsya vicārya kuru yad dhitam
english: Vidura said: 'You are our father, you are our mother, you are our supreme teacher. Therefore deliberate yourself and do what is beneficial for this family.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca atha śuśrāva viprebhyo gāndhārīṃ subalātmajām ārādhya varadaṃ devaṃ bhaganetraharaṃ haram gāndhārī kila putrāṇāṃ śataṃ lebhe varaṃ śubhā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then from brahmins he (Bhīṣma) heard of Gāndhārī, daughter of Subala — that she had propitiated the god who grants boons, Hara the destroyer of Bhaga’s eyes, and that the auspicious Gāndhārī had obtained a boon of a hundred sons.
